subject: Configurable retention profiles + per-region storage: API & rollout asks
messages:
From: Emma Chen <emma@finedge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: tenant-level retention + region pinning via API

Hi Ben / Soojin,

Quick ask from our security and infra teams as we evaluate Redwood for production: can we set retention rules per workspace (not just org-wide), and independently pin storage residency per workspace/tenant to EU regions? Ideally we'd like an admin API to programmatically set a "retention profile" (TTL, soft-delete window, backup retention) and a separate storage-residency flag that forces all object storage + logs to EU regions only.

A couple of specifics:
- We need retention granularity: 30d / 90d / 1y / infinite, plus a configurable soft-delete hold of 30 days before purge.
- Storage residency must support a policy fallback so if EU capacity is constrained it fails with a clear error (we cannot fall back to non-EU).
- Audit logging showing the effective retention and residency per tenant would be required for compliance.

Attaching a simple matrix for what we need (retention_matrix_v1.xlsx). Can you share if this is on Redwood's roadmap and what the expected timeline and API surface would look like? Also who on product/engineering should we coordinate with to validate security controls?

Thanks — Emma
Emma Chen
Head of Security, FinEdge Labs

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Chen <emma@finedge.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: tenant-level retention + region pinning via API

Emma, thanks — great level of detail, this is exactly the sort of ask we anticipate from EU-regulated fintechs. I've looped in Lauren (product) and Soojin (solutions/reliability) so we can line up an initial plan and scope.

Quick next steps:
1) Lauren — can you confirm whether "per-tenant retention profiles + per-tenant residency pinning" is on the roadmap or an extension request, and what the rough priority would be?
2) Soojin — can you surface any constraints (KV cache, cross-region KV writes, backup paths) that would block strict residency-only enforcement?
3) Emma — would you be able to share an internal security checklist or the specific audit fields you need in logs? The attachment you sent is helpful.

I'll arrange a 30-minute sync for next week if that works.

—Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Emma Chen <emma@finedge.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: tenant-level retention + region pinning via API

Emma / Ben — quick technical notes from infra:
- We currently support tenant-level metadata and can tag tenant objects with region tags, but there is no enforcement path today that returns an error when a non-EU region would be selected.
- Hard-blocking fallback will require a new routing policy layer + an enforcement check in the placement service; estimate: 2–3 sprints to prototype, 3–6 sprints to productize for limited capacity.
- Retention TTL per-tenant is feasible; soft-delete window and audit fields require changes to our lifecycle engine and audit schema.

I can sketch a minimal API (PUT /v1/tenants/{id}/retention_profile) that accepts TTL + soft_delete_days + residency_tag. But we need product to define the allowed enums and failure modes (e.g., reject request if residency_tag unavailable).

Sooj
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Emma Chen <emma@finedge.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: tenant-level retention + region pinning via API

Hi all — thanks, Emma, for the detailed matrix and Ben / Soojin for the quick triage. Bringing product & engineering alignment here.

Summary of proposal (short):
- Feature: Retention Profiles (per-tenant) + Residency Pinning (per-tenant).
- API surface (proposal):
  * GET /v1/tenants/{tid}/retention_profile
  * PUT /v1/tenants/{tid}/retention_profile { retention_ttl: enum(30d,90d,1y,inf), soft_delete_days: int, purge_policy: enum(immediate, delayed), residency: enum(eu,us,apac,none) }
  * GET /v1/tenants/{tid}/residency_status -> current placement + fallback status
- Enforcement semantics:
  * residency=eu => reject placement outside eu; return 409 with explanation if capacity unavailable. No silent fallback.
  * retention TTL enforced by lifecycle worker; soft-delete window exposed in audit trail.
- Observability / audit
  * Add tenant_retention_profile field to token-level billing traces and to request logs.
  * Audit export link: exportable CSV for compliance with timestamp and actor.

Rough roadmap & priorities (estimates):
- Discovery + API design: 2 weeks (include FinEdge and security review)
- Prototype enforcement & residency routing: 2 sprints (infra prototype)
- Lifecycle + audit changes: 2 sprints in parallel with proto
- Beta: +2 sprints for limited customers + doc/SDK work
-> Total to first-beta: approx 10–12 weeks, contingent on prioritization.

Deliverables I'll own for the next milestone: detailed API contract (OpenAPI fragment), a migration plan for existing tenants, and a compliance checklist for FinEdge to review. I attached a draft spec link and the retention matrix Ben forwarded.

Action items:
- Ben: schedule a 30-min kickoff with FinEdge + product + infra (please propose 3 slots)
- Soojin: can you list the exact infra config flags we need to add to the placement service by EOD Monday?
- Emma: please confirm whether FinEdge requires immutable retention (no admin override) or tolerates admin-updates with audit.

I'll share the API fragment by next Wednesday. 

—Lauren
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: retention_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx)
Document: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1X-retention-profiles-spec
